purpose: Validate whether the exact technically approved claim wording is supported by the recorded source locators without promoting corroborated-only locators to artifact-verified status.
invariants: Citation validation applies to approved_claim_text from the human technical-review decision artifact, not superseded original wording.
A claim is citation-validated only when at least one verified source/locator directly supports the approved wording without depending on an unverified required source.
Supplementary unverified sources do not block validation when a verified primary source independently supports the entire approved claim.
Corroborated Navy locators remain non-validated until the exact official artifact is captured and verified.
Citation validation does not constitute instructional review, final approval, scoring approval, question approval, or assessment eligibility.

validations.approved_claim_text: High‑current ground strap maintains low resistance
validations.validation_basis: The Coalinga page supports connection/corrosion context but not the full high-current ground-path proposition. The Navy locator supplies the needed ground-return voltage-drop support, but the exact official artifact remains uncaptured and unhashed.

sources.locator: Section 4.06: corroded terminals and connection cleaning
sources.support_scope: Supports corrosion/connection-condition context only; no universal ground-path resistance or voltage-drop threshold.

sources.locator: Section 1.3.4, printed 8-21: voltage drop along the ground return
sources.support_scope: Needed for the specific high-current ground-return/voltage-drop concept. Search-indexed text corroborates the locator, but exact artifact verification is still unavailable.

validations.validation_basis: DOE-HDBK-1084-95 directly supports automotive SLI charging characteristics, partial-float charging while the vehicle is running, charger-to-battery matching, and dependence on application conditions. Navy material is supplementary, not required for this broad approved wording.

sources.locator: Applications > Starting, Lighting, and Ignition, p. 23; Maintenance > Matching the Charger to Battery Requirements, p. 29
sources.support_scope: Direct support for general lead-acid/SLI charging characteristics and charger matching.

sources.locator: Section 1.2.4, printed 8-17: charging voltage against manufacturer specification
sources.support_scope: Supplementary automotive charging-system context only; not required to validate the broad approved claim.

validations.validation_basis: DOE-HDBK-1084-95 directly states that a discharged lead-acid battery may initially accept high charging current and that current must decrease as full charge is approached; under constant-voltage charging, charge current falls as battery voltage rises.

sources.locator: Maintenance > Matching the Charger to Battery Requirements, p. 29; Operation and Construction, pp. 13 to 20
sources.support_scope: Direct support for general charging-current behavior; no universal automotive amperage threshold is inferred.

validations.approved_claim_text: Electrical charging demand and belt-driven auxiliaries increase mechanical load on the engine.
validations.validation_basis: The verified Frontiers article defines auxiliary engine loads as equipment drawing power from the engine and quantifies alternator plus belt-driven auxiliary power demand. This directly supports the approved revised directional claim.

sources.locator: Full text; p. 7 candidate chunks: auxiliary load power demand
sources.support_scope: Direct support that alternator and belt-driven auxiliary demand imposes mechanical power demand on the engine.

sources.locator: Chapter 3, printed pp. 10 to 17; Chapter 5, printed pp. 18 to 28: charging output under load tests
sources.support_scope: Supplementary charging-output-under-load context; military numeric procedures are not generalized.

validations.approved_claim_text: If charging-system output is insufficient under the specified electrical load, system voltage may fall below the manufacturer-specified range.
validations.validation_basis: Army and Frontiers sources support load-testing and electrical-demand context, but the exact generic statement tying insufficient output under specified load to voltage falling below the manufacturer-specified range depends materially on the Navy locator. That locator is corroborated but not artifact-verified.

sources.locator: Section 1.3.1, printed 8-19: output and load testing
sources.support_scope: Needed for the manufacturer-specification under-load diagnostic relationship; exact official artifact remains unavailable.

sources.locator: Chapter 5, printed pp. 18 to 28: alternator output tests
sources.support_scope: Supports charging-output testing under load, but military procedures do not establish a generic manufacturer-specification statement.

sources.locator: Full text; p. 7 candidate chunks: auxiliary load power demand
sources.support_scope: Supports auxiliary power-demand context, not the diagnostic voltage-below-specification conclusion.
